description:
EXOVAND is a team of passionate, curious, and innovative minds united by a shared interest in space, science, and technology. As participants in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to explore real-world challenges, think beyond boundaries, and transform creative ideas into meaningful solutions.
Our team believes in teamwork, innovation, problem-solving, and learning through exploration.
summary:
Team EXOVAND developed the Mars & Moon Analog Globe, an interactive platform that explores locations on Earth with geological and environmental similarities to the Moon and Mars.

Our project addresses the challenge of identifying Earth locations that can serve as analog environments for future lunar bases and Martian exploration. The website features an interactive globe containing 10 selected analog sites across different parts of the world. Users can explore locations, search for sites, and discover their geological characteristics.

The platform also includes a Mission Lab with three tools: Similarity Meter, Compare Two Sites, and Location Filter. These features help users estimate similarities between locations and explore which environments may be useful for specific mission requirements.

Our accompanying PDF presentation explains the challenge, selected locations, comparisons, methodology, and conclusions. Similarity scores are project estimates rather than measured scientific values.

Our goal is to show how Earth can serve as a natural testing ground for understanding other worlds and preparing for future space exploration.

Team: EXOVAND
details: EXOVAND – Mars & Moon Analog Globe NASA International Space Apps Challenge 2026 Challenge: Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars. Project Overview Team EXOVAND developed the Mars & Moon Analog Globe, an interactive platform that explores real locations on Earth with geological and environmental characteristics similar to selected regions of Mars and the Moon. Our project focuses on the idea that Earth can serve as a natural testing ground for planetary exploration. By identifying and characterizing analog environments, we can better understand the challenges future lunar and Martian missions may face. Problem Statement Before exploring other worlds, scientists and mission planners need to understand their terrain and environmental conditions. Testing equipment and methods in relevant Earth environments can help prepare for future missions. However, many potential analog locations are not easy to discover, explore or compare. Our platform brings selected Earth analog environments together in one accessible interactive experience. Our Solution We created an interactive globe featuring Mars and Moon analog locations around the world. Users can switch between Mars and Moon, rotate and zoom the globe, select location markers, and explore information about each site. The project includes five Mars analog entries and five Moon analog entries, with Devon Island represented for both worlds. Selected Analog Locations Mars: Lonar Crater (India), Lake Sandvatn (Iceland), Yana–Indigirka Lowland (Russia), Holuhraun Lava Field (Iceland), and McMurdo Dry Valleys (Antarctica). Moon: Mistastin Lake (Canada), Nördlinger Ries Crater (Germany), Sudbury Impact Structure (Canada), Pinacate Volcanic Field (Mexico), and Devon Island/Haughton Crater (Canada). These locations represent features such as impact craters, basaltic lava, volcanic terrain, polar deserts, polygonal ground and ice-rich environments. Main Website Features - Interactive 3D globe with selectable location markers. - Separate Mars and Moon exploration modes. - Search by location, country, mineral or geological feature. - Location information including temperature, pressure, minerals and geological characteristics. - Mission Lab for comparing and evaluating analog sites. Mission Lab The Mission Lab contains three main tools: 1. Similarity Meter: Estimates how closely an Earth location matches selected Mars or Moon conditions. 2. Compare Two Sites: Allows users to compare two analog locations side by side. 3. Location Filter: Recommends potential analog sites based on the selected world, mission activity and environmental conditions. Our presentation includes example estimates, such as Devon Island's 67% similarity to Mars and the comparison of McMurdo Dry Valleys and Holuhraun. These scores are project estimates, not measured scientific values. Data Sources and Research Our project draws on open resources and references from NASA Earthdata, NASA Worldview, NASA Planetary Data System, ESA, JAXA, CSA, Copernicus and ISRO, along with location-specific geological and climate references. Limitations No Earth environment can fully reproduce the Moon's vacuum or Mars's thin atmosphere, low gravity and radiation conditions. Our analog locations represent selected geological and environmental similarities rather than exact planetary equivalents. Expected Impact The Mars & Moon Analog Globe aims to make planetary analog research more accessible, help users understand the similarities and differences between Earth and other worlds, and demonstrate how Earth environments can support preparation for future space exploration. Team: EXOVAND Project tagline: Earth is our laboratory for the Moon and Mars.
